claims.text: Machine-learning potentials trained on ab initio data can accurately predict fusion properties.
Machine-learning potentials trained on ab initio data can accurately predict high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
Machine-learning potentials would have lower computational cost than explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
Machine-learning potentials would have lower computational cost than TOR-TILD.
The proposed intervention is to train machine-learning potentials on ab initio data.
Machine-learning potentials can capture the complex interactions relevant to fusion and high-temperature thermodynamics.
Machine-learning potentials can retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling sufficiently for the proposed predictions.
The intervention would increase throughput for predicting fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed temperature boundary is above 1000 K.
The stated composition boundary is elemental and binary systems.
The proposed method is intended for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
Limited training data and bias in machine-learning potentials may reduce predictive fidelity.
Failure to reproduce benchmark phase free energies and derived observables within an error tolerance exemplified as 10% would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions identify multicomponent high-entropy systems as the target, whereas the explicit composition boundary and initial-state description restrict the scope to elemental and binary systems.
